world_art_prompt.scene: Key art of the fantasy world 'Chain Delta' at dusk, high three-quarter aerial view: a vast annular wetland of floating triangular stone platforms over dark still water, each triangle's edges marked with small glowing amber arrows. At the very center, a conspicuous round hole of empty dark water that nothing covers. Beyond the wetland rises the 'Degree Dynamo', a hill of great brass spheres turning on axles with gold lightning between them, and in the far distance a domed fortress built around a hollow stone ball. Mist hangs between the triangles. Gyroid stands on a triangle at the edge holding a glowing gold blade of light. Small violet creatures lurk among the tiles.

art.prompt: Annular wetland of oriented triangle platforms around an uncovered central hole; the Degree Dynamo's turning spheres beyond; a domed fortress around a hollow ball; Gyroid with a gold blade.

map.note: World 2 overworld layout (map units). Sites are places; paths are routes; gates need earlier tools.

sites.name: Delta Mouth
sites.note: Where the causeway from the Commutator's Keep descends into the wetland.

sites.name: The Empty Middle
sites.note: The uncovered hole at the delta's center — no triangle fills it, so the cycle around it survives.

gate.note: A stone tile blocks the way: cut it to its boundary with the Boundary Blade — interior edges cancel and the passage opens.
A rope bridge of tangled words: re-tie it with the Clasp.
The Dynamo sits on a raised plateau: sling up with the Suspension Sling.
The dome's lock is a sphere: turn it to the right degree with the Degree Dial.

2-1.site: Tile Yard — the delta's edge, where triangle platforms are stacked, labeled with arrows and glued together.
2-1.story: Chain Delta is built from triangles whose edges carry arrows. Before Gyroid can count holes of every dimension he must learn how places are built from ordered triangles: two triangles make a torus, a Klein bottle or a projective plane, depending only on how their arrows are matched.
2-1.objective: Assemble surfaces from triangles by matching arrowed edges.
mechanics: Triangle crane: pick triangles up and lower them so their edges meet; edges glue only if arrows agree (vertices are ordered, and every edge runs from lower to higher vertex).
Glue preview: after gluing, the crane shows the resulting surface floating above the yard.
Vertex count: identified corners fuse into one; the yard tallies vertices, edges and triangles (χ, from 0-4).
2-1.math_check: Δ-complexes: simplices with ordered vertices, faces glued by order-preserving identifications; the torus, Klein bottle and RP² each from two triangles (Hatcher pp. 102–104).

stages.name: Two Triangles
stages.description: Glue two triangles along one edge into a square.

stages.name: The Torus
stages.description: Glue the square's opposite edges with matching arrows: a torus — one vertex, three edges, two triangles.

stages.name: Flip an Arrow
stages.description: Same square, one pair reversed: a Klein bottle. Both pairs crossed: a projective plane.

stages.name: Wrong Order
stages.description: Repair Null's sabotaged yard, where arrows were relabeled so that gluings no longer respect vertex order.

enemies.name: Flipper
enemies.description: New: a violet frog that hops onto an edge and reverses its arrow; one lash.

2-1.tools: Uses the Cell-Smith (gluing) and the Lash.
2-1.music: Chain Delta theme: a hushed 84 bpm piece in E minor, marimba arpeggios over a low drone, water drips on the offbeat — first statement.
2-1.visuals: Dusk wetland, floating stone triangle platforms with glowing amber arrows on their edges, a brass crane, a translucent torus forming overhead.

2-2.site: Cancel Marsh — a marsh of tiled triangles, some fused into larger plazas.
2-2.story: Emmy forges the Boundary Blade: cut anything along its edge, with arrows, and shared interior edges cancel. Cut a boundary again and nothing is left — every time. A loop that is not the edge of anything is a cycle that survives: a hole.
2-2.objective: Use the Boundary Blade to find cycles, boundaries, and the holes left between them.
mechanics: Boundary Blade (new): strike a tile or a patch of tiles; its boundary lights as an arrowed loop, interior shared edges cancelling (one arrow each way).
Strike again: the boundary of a boundary is always empty — the blade passes through without a mark (∂∂ = 0).
Cycles: chains with no boundary. Boundaries: cycles that are edges of something. Holes: cycles that are not boundaries.
Hole meter: the meter counts surviving cycle classes in each dimension (cycles modulo boundaries).
2-2.math_check: Simplicial chains Cₙ, ∂ with alternating signs, ∂∂ = 0, Hₙ = ker ∂ₙ / im ∂ₙ₊₁ (Hatcher pp. 104–108).

stages.name: First Cut
stages.description: Strike one triangle: three arrowed edges light.

stages.name: Shared Edges
stages.description: Strike a plaza of triangles: the interior edges cancel and only the outer boundary remains.

stages.name: Nothing Left
stages.description: Strike the boundary itself: nothing — every vertex appears once with + and once with −.

stages.name: The Missing Tile
stages.description: A ring of tiles around a missing one: its inner loop is a cycle but not a boundary. Count H₁.

enemies.name: Flipper
enemies.description: Reverses arrows so edges stop cancelling.

enemies.name: Bog spawn
enemies.description: New: a violet blob that fills in missing tiles, hiding holes; two lashes (it is 2-dimensional).

2-2.music: Chain Delta theme with a soft bell for every cancelling edge pair.
2-2.visuals: A marsh of triangle tiles; a glowing gold blade leaving arrowed outlines; pairs of opposite arrows dissolving into sparks; a dark gap where one tile is missing.

2-3.site: Singular Shallows — misty shallows where triangles can be bent, crumpled and collapsed into any shape.
2-3.story: Real places don't come with tidy triangles. In the Shallows, any map of a triangle counts — even crumpled ones. Homology built from all of them gives the same answer as the tidy count, and places that deform into each other (0-3) have the same homology.
2-3.objective: Measure holes with crumpled triangles, and see that deforming a place never changes its homology.
mechanics: Singular stamps: stamp a triangle into the shallows along any map — stretched, folded or squashed to a line.
The Boundary Blade works on stamps exactly as on tiles.
Deform test: slide a place with the Tide Glass (0-2) or retract it (0-1); the hole meter doesn't change.
Path components: the meter's H₀ counts separate pieces.
2-3.math_check: Singular homology; H₀ counts path components; homotopy-equivalent spaces have isomorphic homology; it agrees with simplicial homology on Δ-complexes (Hatcher pp. 108–113; the agreement is proved on p. 128).

stages.name: Any Triangle
stages.description: Stamp crumpled triangles; the blade still cuts their edges.

stages.name: Pieces
stages.description: Count separate islands with H₀.

stages.name: Bend, Don't Change
stages.description: Retract a fat annulus to its core circle: the meter stays at one 1-dimensional hole.

stages.name: Same Shape, Same Count
stages.description: Bring back the Mirror Couriers (0-3): equivalent places read identically on every meter.

enemies.name: Mirror spawn
enemies.description: From 0-3: copies a place in a lumpier shape.

enemies.name: Crumpler
enemies.description: New: a violet wad that stamps degenerate triangles to confuse the meter; one lash.

2-3.tools: Uses the Boundary Blade, Tide Glass and Spool.
2-3.music: Chain Delta theme slowed and blurred with reverb, like hearing it through fog.
2-3.visuals: Misty shallows; gold triangles crumpled, folded and stretched like cloth; the meter floating as a glowing abacus (no numerals).

2-4.site: Chase Channels — canals arranged in long rows of locks, each lock feeding the next.
2-4.story: Water flows from lock to lock; whatever leaves one is exactly what the next one drains — an exact sequence. Gyroid learns to chase a drop of water through the grid, and to read a place's homology from a pair: the place and a part of it.
2-4.objective: Chase elements through lock diagrams and use the long exact sequence of a pair.
mechanics: Locks are groups; sluices are maps. A row is exact where the water entering a lock is exactly what the next sluice discards.
Diagram chase: carry a drop down, across and back up the grid; each move must follow a sluice or reverse one where exactness allows.
The pair sequence: for a place X and a part A, locks for A, X and (X, A) link into one long chain, joined by the connecting sluice ∂.
Relative cycles: chains in X whose edge lies in A.
2-4.math_check: Exact sequences, short exact sequences of chain complexes give long exact sequences, the long exact sequence of a pair, diagram chasing, the five lemma (Hatcher pp. 113–118).

stages.name: Exact Locks
stages.description: Check exactness lock by lock.

stages.name: The Chase
stages.description: Chase a drop to build the connecting sluice ∂.

stages.name: A Place and a Part
stages.description: Compute the homology of a disk relative to its rim from the pair sequence.

stages.name: Five Locks
stages.description: Two rows joined by sluices; four are known to be perfect transfers: prove the middle one is too.

enemies.name: Leak sprite
enemies.description: New: punctures locks so water escapes and exactness breaks; seal the leak, then lash.

2-4.music: A steady 96 bpm canal-boat groove; each lock adds an instrument as the chase passes through it.
2-4.visuals: Rows of stone canal locks with glowing amber water, sluice gates in grids, a single gold drop tracing a path across the grid.

2-5.site: Excision Cut — the delta's far bank, a quarry where pieces of land can be cut out and collapsed.
2-5.story: Cut out a piece well inside a part and the relative count doesn't change. Collapse a part to a point (0-5) and the relative count becomes ordinary homology. With these, Gyroid finally computes the homology of spheres: a sphere has a hole in exactly one dimension.
2-5.objective: Excise and collapse to compute homology, and find the hole in every sphere.
mechanics: Excision saw: cut a region whose closure sits inside the interior of A; the relative meter stays the same.
Collapse press (0-5 Cone Zone): squash A to a point; for a good pair the relative homology equals the reduced homology of X/A.
Sphere ladder: Dⁿ with its rim collapsed is Sⁿ; climb the ladder using the pair sequence one dimension at a time.
2-5.math_check: Excision; good pairs and H̃(X/A) ≅ H(X, A); H̃ₖ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ for k = n and 0 otherwise; Sᵐ ≇ Sⁿ, ℝᵐ ≇ ℝⁿ for m ≠ n; no retraction Dⁿ → Sⁿ⁻¹ (Hatcher pp. 118–128).

stages.name: Cut Deep
stages.description: Excise a region inside A; the relative meter doesn't flinch.

stages.name: Collapse
stages.description: Squash a disk's rim to a point: a sphere appears on the press.

stages.name: The Ladder
stages.description: Climb from S¹ to S³, carrying the single hole up one dimension each rung.

stages.name: Too Close to the Edge
stages.description: Null's saw cuts a region touching A's edge; show why excision fails there, then fix the cut.

enemies.name: Quarry golem
enemies.description: New: a violet stone hulk that welds excised pieces back; three lashes.

2-5.tools: Uses the Boundary Blade, Suspension Sling and Collapse press.
2-5.music: Chain Delta theme with quarry percussion (stone clacks) and a rising figure on each rung of the ladder.
2-5.visuals: A stone quarry on the far bank; glowing gold saw cuts; a press squashing a disk's rim into a point to form a sphere; a ladder of nested spheres.

2-6.site: Dynamo Gate — the base of the Degree Dynamo, where great brass spheres turn on axles and wrap around each other.
2-6.story: Null's sphere claimed loops were blind to its hollow. Homology isn't: H₂ of the sphere is ℤ. Each dynamo maps a sphere onto a sphere; its degree counts how many times. The antipodal dynamo flips orientation in odd dimensions, and no wind can blow over a sphere without a calm spot.
2-6.objective: Refute Null's World 1 claim, measure degrees of sphere maps, and comb the hairy ball.
mechanics: Degree Dial (new): set on a dynamo, it shows how many times the source sphere wraps its target (via H_n).
Reflections have degree −1; compositions multiply degrees; maps that slide into each other have equal degree.
Antipodal dynamo: degree (−1)ⁿ⁺¹ on Sⁿ.
Wind comb: try to set wind arrows on every tile of a sphere island with no calm spot; on S² it can't be done.
2-6.math_check: H₂(S²) ≅ ℤ (refutes the World 1 claim that S² has no hole); degree of maps Sⁿ → Sⁿ, properties, antipodal map has degree (−1)ⁿ⁺¹; Sⁿ has a nowhere-zero tangent vector field iff n is odd (Hatcher pp. 134–137).

stages.name: The Hollow, Seen
stages.description: Measure Null's sphere: H₂ = ℤ. The hollow is real.

stages.name: Wrap Count
stages.description: Set dynamos to wrap a sphere 0, 1, 2 and −1 times.

stages.name: Through the Center
stages.description: The antipodal dynamo on circle and sphere: degree +1 on S¹, −1 on S².

stages.name: The Hairy Ball
stages.description: Comb the sphere island: one calm spot always remains. Then comb the circle smoothly.

enemies.name: Winder
enemies.description: From 1-3: now wraps spheres, not just circles.

enemies.name: Gale spawn
enemies.description: New: violet wisps that blow wind across tiles; lash to calm them.

2-6.music: Degree Dynamo theme: an industrial 110 bpm march in A minor, brass stabs on each full wrap, a low turbine hum.
2-6.visuals: Great brass spheres turning on axles, one wrapping a translucent skin around another, gold lightning arcing between them; a sphere island with arrows swirling around a single calm spot.

2-7.site: Cell Block — a fortress-workshop where places are built cell by cell (0-4) and their homology read off the cells.
2-7.story: With a cell structure, homology needs only the cells: one group per dimension, joined by maps whose entries are degrees. Torus, projective plane and Klein bottle reveal their holes in a few lines, and the Euler characteristic from the Timber Yard returns as the alternating count of holes.
2-7.objective: Compute homology from cells and degrees, and check χ against the holes.
mechanics: Cell chain: each dimension's cells are a stack of crates; the attaching maps' degrees (Degree Dial) become arrows between stacks.
Read holes: kernel over image at each stack, as in 2-2.
Torsion: on RP² the 1-cell's boundary runs around twice: H₁ = ℤ₂ — a loop that dies when doubled (1-7).
χ check: alternating sum of cells equals alternating sum of hole ranks.
2-7.math_check: Cellular homology, the cellular boundary formula via degrees, homology of the torus, RP², Klein bottle and CPⁿ; χ = Σ(−1)ⁿ rank Hₙ (Hatcher pp. 137–149).

stages.name: Crates
stages.description: A sphere as one 0-cell and one 2-cell: holes in dimension 0 and 2.

stages.name: The Torus
stages.description: All boundary degrees zero: ℤ, ℤ², ℤ.

stages.name: The Doubled Edge
stages.description: RP²: the 2-cell wraps the edge twice: torsion ℤ₂ appears.

stages.name: Census
stages.description: Verify χ for five places both ways.

2-7.tools: Uses the Cell-Smith, Degree Dial and Spool.
2-7.music: Degree Dynamo theme with Foundry hammers from World 0.
2-7.visuals: A stone fortress-workshop with stacked glowing crates by dimension, gold arrows between stacks, a projective plane forming from a disk with its rim doubled.

2-8.site: Patchwork Fields — fields covered by overlapping canvas patches.
2-8.story: Cover a place with two overlapping patches. Their holes and the overlap's holes link in a long exact sequence: Mayer–Vietoris. It is the homology version of Van Kampen (1-7).
2-8.objective: Compute homology from two overlapping patches.
mechanics: Lay patches A and B over a place so their interiors cover it.
The Mayer–Vietoris locks: overlap → A ⊕ B → whole → (one dimension down) overlap…
Chase through it as in 2-4.
2-8.math_check: The Mayer–Vietoris sequence; homology of Sⁿ by hemispheres; of the torus and Klein bottle by annuli (Hatcher pp. 149–153).

stages.name: Two Hemispheres
stages.description: Cover a sphere by two caps overlapping in a band.

stages.name: Two Annuli
stages.description: Cover the torus by two cylinders.

stages.name: The Twisted Patch
stages.description: Same for the Klein bottle: a twist in the overlap changes the answer.

stages.name: Patch It Yourself
stages.description: Choose your own cover for a new place.

2-8.tools: Uses the Boundary Blade and the Van Kampen Clasp (the patches clip together with it).
2-8.music: Degree Dynamo theme as a folk reel — fiddle-like square wave.
2-8.visuals: Rolling fields under great overlapping canvas patches, glowing gold seams where they overlap.

2-9.site: Mod Mill — a waterwheel mill that grinds counts down mod 2.
2-9.story: Count holes with even-or-odd instead of whole numbers and some surfaces suddenly speak up: a Klein bottle or projective plane, invisible to ℤ in the top dimension, has a top hole mod 2. Arrows stop mattering.
2-9.objective: Compute homology with coefficients and detect non-orientable surfaces.
mechanics: The mill's wheel switches the meter's coefficients between ℤ and ℤ₂ (and ℤₙ).
Mod 2, edge directions don't matter: flipped arrows count the same.
Non-orientable test: H₂ with ℤ₂ is ℤ₂ while H₂ with ℤ is 0.
2-9.math_check: Homology with coefficients; Hₙ(M; ℤ₂) ≅ ℤ₂ for closed connected n-manifolds; Hₙ(M; ℤ) = 0 for non-orientable ones (Hatcher pp. 153–160).

stages.name: Even or Odd
stages.description: Recount the torus mod 2.

stages.name: The Projective Plane
stages.description: H₂ mod 2 lights; H₂ with ℤ doesn't.

stages.name: Flippers Lose
stages.description: Mod 2, Flipper frogs can't disrupt anything.

stages.name: Sort the Surfaces
stages.description: Sort surfaces into orientable and not.

2-9.music: A two-beat waltz with the melody alternating between two notes, mod 2.
2-9.visuals: A stone mill with a huge waterwheel, amber water, a Klein bottle sculpture in the millpond.

2-10.site: Abelian Ford — a shallow ford where the Commutator's ribbon patrols try to cross into the delta.
2-10.story: The Commutator follows Gyroid into the delta. But here H₁ is the abelianization of π₁: order is forgotten, and his word a b a⁻¹ b⁻¹ counts as nothing. His patrols can't pass.
2-10.objective: Use homology to dissolve the Commutator's patrol words.
mechanics: Ford meter: a patrol's word becomes a vector of letter totals (a counts minus a⁻¹ counts, and the same for b).
Commutators total zero: they are boundaries in the ford.
Patrols whose word totals zero dissolve when they enter the ford; others must be lashed.
2-10.math_check: H₁(X) ≅ π₁(X)ᵃᵇ for path-connected X; commutators map to zero (Hatcher pp. 166–168).

stages.name: Totals
stages.description: Read patrol words as totals.

stages.name: Dissolve
stages.description: Lure commutator patrols into the ford.

stages.name: Not Everything Dies
stages.description: A patrol walking a a b survives: its totals are (2, 1).

stages.name: Hold the Ford
stages.description: Defend the ford against a mixed wave.

enemies.name: Ribbon patrol
enemies.description: From World 1: dissolves in the ford if its totals are zero.

enemies.name: The Commutator (cameo)
enemies.description: Watches from the far bank and withdraws.

2-10.tools: Uses the Van Kampen Clasp and Boundary Blade.
2-10.music: The Commutator's fugue, collapsing into the Chain Delta theme as order is forgotten.
2-10.visuals: A shallow ford with amber water, ribbon guards dissolving into ripples as they cross, the Commutator on the far bank.

2-B1.site: Jordan Ring — an island ringed by a single closed wall.
2-B1.story: Classic results with Gyroid's new tools: any closed wall in the plane splits it into an inside and an outside; open sets of the same dimension can't be squeezed into different shapes; and only a few dimensions allow division.
2-B1.objective: Prove the wall has an inside, using homology.
mechanics: Draw any closed wall (no self-crossing) with the Spool; the meter reports two regions.
Invariance of domain demo: a squeezed open patch remains open.
2-B1.math_check: Jordan curve theorem (via Sⁿ minus an embedded sphere), invariance of domain, a commutative division algebra structure on ℝⁿ exists only for n = 1, 2 (Hatcher pp. 169–177). Flag: the full 1, 2, 4, 8 theorem needs K-theory beyond Ch. 2; the game only mentions it.

stages.name: Draw a Wall
stages.description: Any wall: two sides.

stages.name: Wild Walls
stages.description: Even a wildly wiggly wall splits the plane in two.

2-B1.tools: Uses the Spool and Boundary Blade.
2-B1.music: Harpsichord variation of the Dynamo theme.
2-B1.visuals: A round island ringed by a single wiggly glowing wall, inside lit gold, outside dark.

2-B2.site: Lefschetz Lantern — a lighthouse whose beam maps the island onto itself.
2-B2.story: The lantern's beam maps a place to itself. Add up the traces of the induced maps on homology: if the total isn't zero, some point maps to itself — a generalization of Brouwer (1-4).
2-B2.objective: Compute Lefschetz numbers and find fixed points.
mechanics: Lantern beam: a map f of the island to itself, shown as arrows.
Trace tally: the tally sums traces of f_* with alternating signs.
Nonzero tally guarantees a lit fixed point; zero tally allows a fixed-point-free map (e.g., rotating a circle).
2-B2.math_check: Simplicial approximation; the Lefschetz fixed point theorem for finite simplicial complexes or their retracts (Hatcher pp. 177–184).

stages.name: Trace
stages.description: Rotate a circle: tally zero, no fixed point needed.

stages.name: Always a Fixed Point
stages.description: Any map of a disk or projective plane has tally 1: find the point.

2-B2.visuals: A stone lighthouse on a point, its gold beam sweeping arrows across the island, one arrow-free glowing spot.

castle.site: The Retractor — Null's dome built around a hollow stone ball; his engine tries to squash the solid ball onto its surface.
castle.story: Null rebuilds his Retractor, one dimension up: crush the whole ball onto its skin. If it worked, the sphere's hole would come from a ball that has none. Gyroid proves it can't work, and Null flees to the gardens.

phases.name: The ball
phases.description: Null's engine squeezes the ball's interior toward its skin. Measure: H₂ of the ball is 0, H₂ of the sphere is ℤ. Tests 2-5.

phases.name: The skin
phases.description: Null's sphere-shields spin; set the Degree Dial to match and reverse each shield's degree to break it. Tests 2-6.

phases.name: The cells
phases.description: Null rebuilds the ball from cells to hide a hole; compute cellular homology to expose that it has none. Tests 2-7.

phases.name: Seize
phases.description: The engine would turn the sphere's hole into nothing and back: it seizes. Null escapes.

castle.tools: Boundary Blade, Degree Dial, Cell-Smith, Suspension Sling.
castle.music: The Retractor's drone from 1-4, an octave lower, with Null's theme on organ; the delta theme breaks through when the engine seizes.
castle.visuals: A stone dome around a huge hollow ball, violet chains pulling at its surface, gold measurement rings orbiting.
castle.movie: castle-2-intro “The Retractor, Again” and castle-2-outro “Classes Multiply”.

2-1.scene: Level 'Tile and Error' in the Tile Yard: a dusk wetland where floating stone triangle platforms with glowing amber arrows along their edges are stacked and moved by a brass crane. Two triangles glued into a square hang from the crane; above them a translucent glowing torus forms. Gyroid guides the crane. A small violet frog sits on an edge.

2-2.scene: Level 'Boundary Issues' in Cancel Marsh: a marsh of stone triangle tiles over dark water. Gyroid swings a glowing gold blade of light; it leaves a glowing arrowed outline around a plaza of triangles, with sparks where interior opposite arrows cancel. In the middle of a ring of tiles, one tile is missing, leaving a dark gap. A violet blob oozes toward the gap.

2-3.scene: Level 'Any Simplex Will Do' in the Singular Shallows: misty shallow water; glowing gold triangles are stretched, folded and crumpled like cloth over the water. A glowing abacus floats in the air. Gyroid stamps a triangle into the shallows. A violet crumpled wad creature lurks.

2-4.scene: Level 'Chase Scene' in the Chase Channels: rows of stone canal locks arranged in a grid, glowing amber water in each, sluice gates between them. A single bright gold drop traces a path down, across and up the grid. Gyroid runs along a lock wall. A violet sprite punctures a lock.

2-5.scene: Level 'Cut and Paste' at the Excision Cut: a stone quarry on a river bank; glowing gold saw cuts in the rock; a great press squashing the rim of a stone disk into a single point so it bulges into a sphere; a ladder of nested glowing spheres climbing up. Gyroid operates the press. A violet stone golem lurks.

2-6.scene: Level 'The Third Degree' at the Degree Dynamo: great brass spheres turning on axles, one wrapping a translucent skin twice around another, gold lightning arcing between them. In the foreground a small sphere island covered in glowing wind arrows swirling around a single calm spot. Gyroid holds a glowing dial. Count Null's pale sphere visible far away.

2-7.scene: Level 'Cell Block': a stone fortress-workshop with glowing crates stacked in three columns, gold arrows between the columns; in the center a disk whose rim is being wrapped around twice to form a projective plane. Gyroid works with a brass-and-indigo gauntlet.

2-8.scene: Level 'Patchwork' in Patchwork Fields: rolling fields under two great overlapping canvas patches held up on poles, glowing gold seams where they overlap; under them, a torus-shaped hill. Gyroid clips two patches together with a copper clasp.

2-9.scene: Level 'Mod Squad' at the Mod Mill: a stone mill with a huge waterwheel turning in amber water; in the millpond, a glass Klein bottle sculpture glowing faintly. Gyroid stands on the mill bridge. A violet frog sits harmlessly on a lily pad.

2-10.scene: Level 'Forget the Order' at the Abelian Ford: a wide shallow river ford with amber-lit water; tall violet guards with loop-shaped pauldrons dissolve into ripples as they try to cross. On the far bank the Commutator watches. Gyroid stands mid-ford.

2-B1.scene: Bonus level 'Classic Moves' at the Jordan Ring: a round island ringed by a single wildly wiggly glowing gold wall; inside lit warm gold, outside dark blue. Gyroid stands on the wall.

2-B2.scene: Bonus level 'Fixed Ideas' at the Lefschetz Lantern: a stone lighthouse on a rocky point at night, its gold beam sweeping across an island covered with gold arrows, one arrow-free glowing spot where the beam rests. Gyroid at the lighthouse door.

castle_art.scene: Castle 'The Retractor': a stone dome built around a huge hollow stone ball; violet chains pull at the ball's surface from a hulking violet machine; glowing gold measurement rings orbit the ball. Count Null (from the reference) stands atop the machine. Gyroid faces him holding a glowing dial and a gold blade.

scenes.title: The yard

scenes.title: Two make a square
scenes.description: The crane lowers two triangles together into a square.

scenes.title: Fold
scenes.description: The square's matching edges curl together: a torus forms. Emmy flips one arrow; the shape twists into a Klein bottle.

scenes.title: Flippers
scenes.description: Violet frogs hop onto edges.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 26: “World 2 · Level 1 — Tile and Error”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: To count holes of every size, we need places built from pieces we can count.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Triangles, with arrows. Edges glue only when the arrows agree.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Two triangles… and it's a torus.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Flip one arrow and it's a Klein bottle. Same pieces, different gluing.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Keep those frogs off my arrows.

videos.title: The Boundary Blade
videos.plays: Before World 2 · Level 2, in Cancel Marsh
videos.synopsis: Emmy forges the Boundary Blade. Cut a patch and shared edges cancel; cut a boundary and nothing is left. A cycle that bounds nothing is a hole.

scenes.title: The forge
scenes.description: Emmy hammers a gold blade of light on a portable anvil at the marsh edge.

scenes.title: First cut
scenes.description: Gyroid strikes a plaza of triangles: inner arrows cancel in sparks, an outline glows.

scenes.title: Nothing left
scenes.description: He strikes the outline: the blade passes through with no mark.

scenes.title: The gap
scenes.description: A ring of tiles around a missing one; the inner loop glows and won't go out.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 28: “World 2 · Level 2 — Boundary Issues”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: My namesake. The Boundary Blade cuts anything down to its edge.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: The inside edges cancel — one arrow each way.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Cut the edge again and… nothing.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: An edge has no edge. Always.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: But a loop that isn't the edge of anything — that's a hole.

videos.title: Any Simplex Will Do
videos.plays: Before World 2 · Level 3, in the Singular Shallows
videos.synopsis: Real places don't come in tidy triangles. Crumpled triangles work too, and places that deform into each other read the same.

scenes.title: Fog
scenes.description: Misty shallows; no tidy tiles anywhere.

scenes.title: Crumpled
scenes.description: Gyroid stamps a triangle that folds like cloth onto the water; the blade still traces its edges.

scenes.title: Same count
scenes.description: A fat annulus slides down to a thin circle; the abacus beads don't move.

scenes.title: Crumplers
scenes.description: Violet wads tumble through the mist.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 26: “World 2 · Level 3 — Any Simplex Will Do”.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: No tiles here. How do we count?

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Any triangle will do — bent, folded, squashed flat. The blade still cuts it.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: And deforming the place doesn't change the count.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Same shape in the Mirror Shoals' sense, same holes.

videos.title: Chase Scene
videos.plays: Before World 2 · Level 4, in the Chase Channels
videos.synopsis: Canal locks pass water exactly from one to the next. Gyroid learns to chase a drop through the grid and read a place's holes from a pair.

scenes.title: The locks
scenes.description: Rows of canal locks glowing amber, sluices between them.

scenes.title: Exact
scenes.description: Water leaves one lock and exactly fills the drain of the next.

scenes.title: The chase
scenes.description: Gyroid follows a gold drop down, across, and up the grid, arriving at a lock no sluice seemed to reach.

scenes.title: Leaks
scenes.description: A violet sprite punctures a lock.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 26: “World 2 · Level 4 — Chase Scene”.

captions.speaker: Narrator
captions.text: In the Chase Channels, nothing was lost between one lock and the next.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: What one sluice sends is exactly what the next one drains. That's exact.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Down, across, back up — the drop found a new route.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: That route links a place's holes to a part's holes. Chase it.

videos.title: Cut and Paste
videos.plays: Before World 2 · Level 5, at the Excision Cut
videos.synopsis: Excise deep inside a part and the relative count holds; collapse a part and it becomes ordinary homology. Climb the sphere ladder.

scenes.title: The quarry
scenes.description: The far bank's quarry; saws and a great press.

scenes.title: Cut deep
scenes.description: A saw removes a block deep inside a marked region; the meter doesn't flinch.

scenes.title: The ladder
scenes.description: The press squashes a disk's rim to a point, making a sphere; spheres stack up a ladder, each with one glowing hole.

scenes.title: Golem
scenes.description: A violet stone golem lumbers out.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 28: “World 2 · Level 5 — Cut and Paste”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Cut out what's deep inside the part, and nothing about the pair changes.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Squash the rim to a point — that's the Cone Zone trick.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And a disk with its rim squashed is a sphere. Climb, and every sphere has exactly one hole.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: One hole, in its own dimension. Null's sphere included.

videos.title: The Third Degree
videos.plays: Before World 2 · Level 6, at the Dynamo Gate
videos.synopsis: Gyroid measures Null's sphere and the hollow is seen. At the Degree Dynamo, maps of spheres wrap a whole number of times — and no wind can cover a sphere without a calm spot.

scenes.title: The hollow
scenes.description: Gyroid points the meter at Null's pale sphere far off; one bead slides into the second row.

scenes.title: Null hears
scenes.description: Null's image flickers, irritated.

scenes.title: The Dynamo
scenes.description: Great brass spheres wrap skins around each other, once, twice, inside-out.

scenes.title: The calm spot
scenes.description: Wind arrows swirl across a sphere island, all but one point.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 30: “World 2 · Level 6 — The Third Degree”.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Loops couldn't see it. The meter can. Your sphere has a hole, Null.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: A number on a dial. Spin it however you like.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The Degree Dial counts how many times one sphere wraps another.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Inside-out counts as minus one.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: And wind can't cover a sphere without a calm spot. Try it.

videos.title: Cell Block
videos.synopsis: Build a place from cells and its holes come from the cells alone. A doubled edge makes a loop that dies when doubled: torsion.

scenes.title: Crates
scenes.description: Glowing crates stacked by dimension; arrows between stacks.

scenes.title: Torus
scenes.description: Torus crates: every arrow reads zero, every crate survives.

scenes.title: Doubled
scenes.description: A disk's rim wraps twice around a loop; the loop glows half-bright.

scenes.title: Census
scenes.description: The Timber Yard census board lights.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 26: “World 2 · Level 7 — Cell Block”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Built cell by cell, a place gives up its holes with almost no work.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: The arrows are just degrees. The Dial reads them.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: The projective plane's disk wraps its edge twice. Go around twice and it's filled.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Once, it's a hole. Twice, it's not. Weird.

videos.title: Patchwork
videos.synopsis: Cover a place with two overlapping patches; their holes and the overlap's link up — Mayer–Vietoris, Van Kampen's cousin.

scenes.title: The fields
scenes.description: Canvas patches over rolling hills.

scenes.title: Two caps
scenes.description: Two caps cover a sphere-hill, overlapping in a band; the seam glows.

scenes.title: Clasp
scenes.description: Gyroid clips patches together with the Clasp.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 24: “World 2 · Level 8 — Patchwork”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Two patches and their overlap tell you the whole place's holes.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Like Van Kampen at the Glue Works — but for holes.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Mind the overlap. That's where the surprises are.

videos.title: Mod Squad
videos.synopsis: Count holes mod 2 and arrows stop mattering — the top hole of a non-orientable surface appears.

scenes.title: The mill
scenes.description: A waterwheel turns; Emmy throws a lever.

scenes.title: Even or odd
scenes.description: The Klein bottle in the pond lights from inside.

scenes.title: Frogs
scenes.description: A Flipper flips an arrow; nothing happens. It looks confused.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 24: “World 2 · Level 9 — Mod Squad”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Count even or odd instead of whole numbers.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: The Klein bottle lit up! It had a hole the whole time?

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Its top hole only shows when arrows don't matter. It has no consistent arrows.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Sorry, frog. Flipping does nothing here.

videos.title: Forget the Order
videos.plays: Before World 2 · Level 10, at the Abelian Ford
videos.synopsis: The Commutator's patrols follow Gyroid into the delta, but in homology order is forgotten and their word counts as nothing.

scenes.title: The ford
scenes.description: Ribbon patrols arrive at a shallow ford.

scenes.title: Dissolve
scenes.description: The first guard steps in, walking a, b, a back, b back; its ribbons dissolve into ripples.

scenes.title: The marshal
scenes.description: The Commutator watches from the far bank, then withdraws.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 26: “World 2 · Level 10 — Forget the Order”.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: The Commutator's patrols followed us.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Here only totals count. a, b, a back, b back totals nothing.

captions.speaker: The Commutator
captions.text: So your counting forgets order. I'll remember that.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: That sounded like a threat.

videos.title: Classic Moves
videos.plays: Before World 2 · Bonus 1, at the Jordan Ring
videos.synopsis: Any closed wall splits the plane into inside and outside — proved with homology.

scenes.title: The wall
scenes.description: A wiggly wall circles an island.

scenes.title: Inside
scenes.description: The inside lights gold, the outside stays dark.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 16: “World 2 · Bonus — Classic Moves”.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Obviously a wall has an inside.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Obvious, and famously hard to prove. Now we have the tools.

videos.title: Fixed Ideas
videos.plays: Before World 2 · Bonus 2, at the Lefschetz Lantern
videos.synopsis: Add up traces on homology; if the total isn't zero, the lantern's map has a fixed point.

scenes.title: The lantern
scenes.description: A lighthouse beam sweeps arrows over the island.

scenes.title: The still spot
scenes.description: The beam rests on one arrow-free spot.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 16: “World 2 · Bonus — Fixed Ideas”.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Brouwer's Basin, grown up: add the traces, find the still point.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Not zero — so somewhere, the beam lands where it started.

videos.title: The Retractor, Again
videos.synopsis: Null has rebuilt his Retractor one dimension up: crush a solid ball onto its sphere skin.

scenes.title: The dome
scenes.description: A stone dome around a hollow ball; violet chains strain at its surface.

scenes.title: Null
scenes.description: Null stands atop the machine, Crown glowing.

scenes.title: Ready
scenes.description: Gyroid raises the Dial; Emmy the meter.

scenes.title: Title
scenes.description: Title card at 28: “World 2 · Castle — The Retractor”.

captions.speaker: Narrator
captions.text: Null had learned nothing from the Basin — only to build bigger.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: A ball is just its skin, stuffed. I'll squeeze out the stuffing.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: Same trick as the Basin. The skin has a hole; the ball doesn't.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: So the engine would have to make a hole out of nothing. Let's watch it try.

videos.title: Classes Multiply
videos.plays: After castle-2 — the end of World 2
videos.synopsis: The Retractor seizes. Null escapes toward the gardens, laughing that the torus and a bouquet with a sphere attached have the same holes. Emmy realizes they need a sharper instrument: holes that multiply.

scenes.title: Seize
scenes.description: The engine's gears grind and lock; chains go slack.

scenes.title: Two islands
scenes.description: Null, escaping, conjures a torus island and a two-loops-plus-sphere island side by side; the meter reads the same on both.

scenes.title: The gardens
scenes.description: Beyond, signal gardens glow with lanterns that light in pairs.

scenes.title: World 2 complete
scenes.description: Card: “World 2 complete — Chain Delta restored.”

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: It's seized. A hole can't come from nothing.

captions.speaker: Count Null
captions.text: Count these, then. Same holes, every dimension. Same place.

captions.speaker: Gyroid
captions.text: The meter agrees with him… but they can't be the same.

captions.speaker: Emmy Boundary
captions.text: Counting holes isn't enough. We need to know how they multiply. To the Gardens.
